rationale: Reached the constructor stall through a live cluster instead of a supplied fixture, which was the main remaining premise of that question. The new harness runs a three-node cluster {A,B,C} in memory with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled on every node, elects B, commits five entries, takes a user snapshot on A at index 6, commits 250 further entries so A's staged commit index reaches 257, shuts A down while B and C keep a quorum, and then restarts A from its own stores with MaxAppendEntries 1. Local construction feedback is deterministic across three runs: the feature-on restart does not return within the 5s window, the cluster stays alive without A, and the identical restart without the feature returns as a follower with lastApplied still at the snapshot index.

scope.description: Live three-node cluster (A, B, C; in-memory transports and stores; timeouts scaled to 50ms) in which node A runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, is snapshotted early at index 6, receives 250 further committed entries so its staged commit index is 257, is shut down while B and C retain a quorum, and is then restarted twice from its own stores: once with the feature and MaxAppendEntries 1, once with the feature off.
assumptions: Every state that matters is produced by normal operations: bootstrap {A,B,C} from A, leader election with leadership transferred to B if needed, committed applies, a user-triggered Snapshot on A, further committed applies, and a graceful Shutdown of A.

The feature is enabled on all three nodes during the first life, which is the deployment mode whose restart behaviour is under test; this is what makes the commit-tracking store hold a persisted commit index for A.
A's snapshot index stays at 6 because SnapshotInterval is 10 minutes and the harness takes no further snapshot on A, so the replay must cover 251 entries.
Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; the control uses the same stores with the feature off so fixture size, store speed and cluster state are excluded as causes.
The stalled constructor is abandoned; a fresh transport is created for each restart attempt and the peers are reconnected to it.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store or process kill is exercised; A is shut down gracefully.
The stalled instance is not resumed and no application-level timeout or supervision is modelled.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds three InmemTransports (A, B, C) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); it bootstraps {A,B,C} from A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, starts A, B and C with MockFSM, waits for a leader and transfers leadership to B if another node won. It applies five commands on the leader, waits until A's applied index is at least four, then takes a user snapshot on A (index 6). It applies 250 further commands, waits until A's log store reports a staged commit index of at least 156, and emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the staged commit index, A's log last index, the number of entries the replay would cover, whether that exceeds the 128-slot channel, the cluster ids and the leader. It shuts A down, confirms the other two nodes still have a leader, and emits 'cluster_status' with whether the cluster is alive without A and whether the stalled restart returned. Each restart attempt creates a fresh transport for A, reconnects the peers, and calls NewRaft in a goroutine with a bounded window: 'stalled_restart' uses Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and MaxAppendEntries 1, 'control_restart' uses the same stores with the feature off. A 'control_restart_summary' event records the control's return and applied index. Event order: fixture, stalled_restart, cluster_status, control_restart, control_restart_summary.
semantic_changes: New harness file: a three-node in-memory cluster with the feature enabled, a user snapshot on one follower, 250 further committed entries, a graceful shutdown of that follower and two restart attempts from its own stores.
The stalled restart uses MaxAppendEntries 1 so 251 entries above the snapshot need 251 batches, and the control restart uses the same stores with the feature off.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft startup path: restoreFromCommittedLogs replays committed entries through processLogs into fsmMutateCh before the constructor starts the only consumer, runFSM.

comparisons.description: A follower restarted with the feature over 251 committed entries should finish NewRaft within the observation window.
Control: the same stores restarted without the feature should construct normally.
Control operand: without the replay the FSM stays at the snapshot index, so the difference is the replay and not the gap itself.
The remaining two voters keep a quorum while the restarted node cannot start, so the stall is not a cluster-wide outage in this size.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft cannot return when the replay needs more batches than the 128-slot fsmMutateCh holds

experiment.revision_reason: Reaches the same stall through ordinary cluster operations rather than a harness-supplied fixture: a follower accumulates a staged commit index far above its last snapshot by running with the feature and then restarting with a small MaxAppendEntries; the comparison set is limited to the new scenario's predicates and the earlier predicates remain with their own receipts.
